name: Benzydamine hydrochloride (mouthwash)
className: Locally acting analgesic and anti-inflammatory for the mouth and throat

formulations.label: Mouthwash / gargle
formulations.strengths: 0.15% w/v benzydamine hydrochloride (22.5 mg per 15 mL dose)
formulations.note: Two UK 0.15% SmPCs used: a mouthwash (mouth and throat, 13 years and over) and a sore throat rinse (throat). Contains ethanol. Expel from the mouth after use.

src.q: Benzydamine hydrochloride 0.15% w/v. Each 15ml dose contains 22.5mg benzydamine hydrochloride.
Benzydamine Hydrochloride 0.15% w/v.
The solution should be expelled from the mouth after use.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Relief of painful inflammatory conditions of the mouth and throat: pharyngitis after tonsillectomy or a nasogastric tube, pharyngitis, aphthous ulcers, oral ulceration due to radiotherapy, and after dental operations.

src.q: A locally acting analgesic and anti-inflammatory treatment for the relief of painful inflammatory conditions of the mouth and throat including:
Pharyngitis following tonsillectomy or the use of a naso-gastric tube.
Pharyngitis, aphthous ulcers and oral ulceration due to radiation therapy. Dentistry: For use after dental operations.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions found in the two UK 0.15% benzydamine SmPCs (pharmacy medicines) or MHRA Drug Safety Update.

items.t: Adults and elderly: rinse or gargle with 15 mL every 1.5 to 3 hours as needed for pain; spit out after use. Do not use continuously for more than 7 days except under medical supervision.

src.q: Rinse or gargle with 15 ml (approximately 1 tablespoonful) every 1½ to 3 hours as required for pain relief.
Uninterrupted treatment should not exceed seven days, except under medical supervision.

items.t: Licensed for children aged 13 years and over (adult dose). Should not be used in children aged 12 years or under.

src.q: is indicated in adults and children aged 13 years and over.
should not be used in children aged 12 years or under.
Not suitable for children aged 12 years or under.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to benzydamine or to any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
Hypersensitivity to the active ingredient, benzydamine hydrochloride or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Not advisable in patients with hypersensitivity to aspirin or other NSAIDs.

src.q: Benzydamine use is not advisable in patients with hypersensitivity to acetylsalicylic acid or other NSAIDs

items.t: Asthma (current or past): bronchospasm may be precipitated; use with caution.

src.q: Bronchospasm may be precipitated in patients suffering from or with a previous history of bronchial asthma. Caution should be exercised in these patients.

items.t: Use undiluted; dilute with water if stinging occurs. Avoid contact with the eyes.

src.q: should generally be used undiluted, but if 'stinging' occurs the rinse may be diluted with water.
Avoid contact with eyes.

items.t: Contains ethanol (one SmPC: 1215 mg per 15 mL) and methyl parahydroxybenzoate, which may cause allergic reactions (possibly delayed).

renal.note: Neither UK 0.15% benzydamine SmPC gives renal advice. Both state systemic absorption of mouthwash doses is relatively low.

hepatic.note: Neither UK 0.15% benzydamine SmPC gives hepatic advice.

items.t: No clinical data. Systemic prostaglandin synthetase inhibitors in the third trimester can harm the fetus. Should not be used during pregnancy unless clearly necessary; if used, keep the dose as low and the course as short as possible.

src.q: During the third trimester of pregnancy, systemic use of prostaglandin synthetase inhibitors may induce cardiopulmonary and renal toxicity in the fetus.
should not be used during pregnancy unless clearly necessary. If used, the dose should be kept as low and duration of treatment as short as possible.

items.t: Should not be used while breastfeeding unless the physician considers it essential.

src.q: should not be used during lactation unless considered essential by the physician.

items.t: No evidence of a teratogenic effect in animal studies (one SmPC). No other fertility information.

src.q: There is no evidence of a teratogenic effect in animal studies.

items.t: Most common: oral numbness and a stinging feeling in the mouth (listed as uncommon).

src.q: The most common side effects are numbness and a stinging feeling in the mouth.
Uncommon Oral numbness (hypothesia) and a stinging feeling in the mouth (oral pain)

items.t: Very rare: itching, urticaria, photosensitivity reaction and rash.

src.q: Very rare Pruritus, urticaria, photosensitivity reaction and rash

items.t: Anaphylactic reactions (potentially life-threatening), angioedema (frequency not known), and very rarely laryngospasm or bronchospasm.

src.q: Anaphylactic reaction which can be potentially life-threatening and hypersensitivity reactions
Very rare Laryngospasm or bronchospasm
Not known Angioedema

items.t: Swallowing large amounts (over 300 mg) can cause gastrointestinal and CNS symptoms (e.g. vomiting, dizziness, hallucinations, agitation); treat symptomatically under close observation.

src.q: Intoxication is only expected in case of accidental ingestion of large quantities of benzydamine (> 300 mg).
Symptoms of the central nervous system include dizziness, hallucinations, agitation, anxiety and irritability.

items.t: Review if continuous treatment would go beyond 7 days: longer use only under medical supervision.

src.q: Uninterrupted treatment should not exceed seven days, except under medical supervision.

items.t: Rinse or gargle with 15 mL using the measuring cup, then spit out. Use undiluted; dilute with water if it stings.
